validated_results.title: Prospective Study of Avocado Consumption and Cancer Risk in U.S. Men and Women.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting hazard ratio for avocado consumption and incident bladder cancer in men.

extraction.comparison_type: Consumption of ≥1 weekly serving of avocados vs lower/no consumption
extraction.population: Men in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study (1986-2016)

sample_size.excerpt: This study included data from 45,289 men in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study (HPFS, 1986-2016) and 67,039 women in the Nurses' Health Study (NHS, 1986-2014).

effect_size.excerpt: In HPFS, consumption of ≥1 weekly serving of avocados was associated with decreased risk of total (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.80-0.91), colorectal (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59-0.85), lung (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90), and bladder cancer (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90).

confidence_interval.excerpt: In HPFS, consumption of ≥1 weekly serving of avocados was associated with decreased risk of total (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.80-0.91), colorectal (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59-0.85), lung (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90), and bladder cancer (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90).

comparison.excerpt: consumption of ≥1 weekly serving of avocados was associated with decreased risk
